newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Mobutu, Kabila differ over how Mobutu steps down.
newsitem.headline: Mobutu, Kabila differ over how Mobutu steps down.

text.p: Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko has agreed to resign but rebel leader Laurent Kabila has rejected a Mobutu proposal to transfer power to a third party, a rebel spokesman said on Sunday,

"Mobutu wants power transferred to another person, who in turn would negotiate with President Kabila, but for us that's unacceptable. Power must go directly to our president," rebel "foreign minister" Bizima Karaha told Reuters by telephone.
"Mobutu has agreed to resign but he wants authority transferred to an interim body and this is what we are negotiating about now," he added.

Karaha was speaking from the South African naval ship the Outeniqua, site of a meeting between Mobutu, Kabila and South African President Nelson Mandela. Karaha confirmed the meeting had started and said the rebels hoped it would end in an announcement that Mobutu was stepping down after more then 30 years in power.
"The three of them are now inside and we shall have more details when they finish. We hope to announce Mobutu's resignation shortly after the meeting," he added.
Kabila told Reuters earlier that he was demanding Mobutu's immediate resignation, otherwise his forces would press on to enter the capital Kinshasa on Sunday evening.
